chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, and from more than one of our companions from Qumm, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-'Amiri, from Abu Sa'id Ghanim al-Hindi, who said:

I was in the city of India known as interior Kashmir, and I had companions who would sit on chairs to the right of the king—forty men, all of whom read the four books: the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur, and the scrolls of Ibrahim. We used to judge between the people, teach them their religion, and give them legal answers regarding their halal and haram. The people would turn to us, from the king down to those beneath him.

Then we discussed the mention of Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and we said: This Prophet mentioned in the books has remained unclear to us, and it is obligatory upon us to investigate him and seek his traces. Our view became united, and we agreed that I should go out and search on their behalf. So I departed with abundant wealth, and traveled for twelve months until I neared Kabul. A group of Turks attacked me, cut me off, took my wealth, wounded me severely, and I was taken to the city of Kabul. When its king learned of my case, he sent me to the city of Balkh, whose governor at that time was Dawud ibn al-'Abbas ibn Abi al-Aswad. News of me reached him—that I had set out from India in search, had learned Persian, and had debated jurists and theologians. So Dawud ibn al-'Abbas sent for me, brought me to his gathering, and assembled the jurists against me. They debated me, and I informed them that I had left my land seeking this Prophet whom I found mentioned in the books.

He said to me: Who is he, and what is his name? I said: Muhammad. They said: He is our Prophet whom you seek. So I asked them about his laws, and they informed me. Then I said to them: I know that Muhammad is a Prophet, but I do not know whether he is this one whom you describe or not. So tell me where he is, that I may go to him and ask him about signs and proofs that I have. If he is the one I have sought, I will believe in him.

They said: He has passed away صلى الله عليه وآله. I said: Then who is his legatee and successor? They said: Abu Bakr. I said: Name him for me, for that is his kunyah. They said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman, and they traced his lineage to Quraysh. I said: Then give me the lineage of Muhammad, your Prophet. So they gave it to me. Then I said: This is not the one I sought. The one I seek is his successor, his brother in religion, his cousin in lineage, the husband of his daughter, and the father of his offspring. This Prophet has no progeny on the earth other than the children of this man who is his successor.

He said: Then they sprang at me and said: O Amir, this man has gone out from shirk into kufr; his blood is lawful. So I said to them: O people, I am a man who has a religion to which I hold fast, and I will not leave it until I see something stronger than it. I found the description of this man in the books that Allah sent down upon His Prophets, and I only left the lands of India and the honor in which I had been for the sake of seeking him. So when I investigated the matter of your companion whom you mentioned, he was not the Prophet described in the books. So they refrained from me.

The governor sent for a man called al-Husayn ibn Ishkib and summoned him. He said to him: Debate this Indian man. Al-Husayn said to him: May Allah set you aright, you have jurists and scholars with you, and they are more knowledgeable and more perceptive in debating him. He said to him: Debate him as I tell you, be alone with him, and treat him gently.

Then al-Husayn ibn Ishkib said to me, after I had spoken with him: The one you seek is indeed the Prophet whom these people described, but the matter of his successor is not as they said. This Prophet is Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and his legatee is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. He is the husband of Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, and the father of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, the two grandsons of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.

Ghanim Abu Sa'id said: So I said: Allah is the Greatest! This is the one I sought. Then I went back to Dawud ibn al-'Abbas and said to him: O Amir, I have found what I sought, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. He said: So he treated me kindly and provided for me, and said to al-Husayn: Look after him. He said: So I stayed with him until I became at ease with him, and he instructed me in what I needed of salat, sawm, and the obligations.

He said: Then I said to him: We read in our books that Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله is the Seal of the Prophets, there is no prophet after him, and that the authority after him belongs to his legatee, his heir, and his successor after him, then to the legatee after the legatee. The command of Allah continues in their descendants until the world comes to an end. So who is the legatee of the legatee of Muhammad? He said: al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, the two sons of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله. Then he continued the matter of the succession until he ended with Sahib al-Zaman عليه السلام. He informed me of what had occurred, and I had no concern except seeking the region. Then he came to Qumm and sat with our companions in the year two hundred and sixty-four, and went out with them until he reached Baghdad, and with him was a companion from the people of Sind who accompanied him upon the madhhab.

Then he said: Ghanim narrated to me, saying: I found some of my companion's character objectionable, so I separated from him and went on until I reached al-'Abbāsiyyah. I prepared for salat and prayed, and while I was standing reflecting on what I had intended in seeking him, suddenly a man came to me and said: Are you so-and-so, by the name known in India? I said: Yes. He said: Answer your Mawla. So I went with him, and he kept taking me through the streets until he came to a house and a garden, and there he عليه السلام was sitting.

He said: Welcome, O so-and-so, in the Indian language. How are you, and how did you leave so-and-so and so-and-so? until he counted all forty of them and asked me about them one by one. Then he informed me of what we had discussed, all of that in the Indian language. Then he said: You intended to perform hajj with the people of Qumm? I said: Yes, my master. He said: Do not perform hajj with them. Return this year, and perform hajj in the coming year.

Then he tossed to me a purse that was before him and said to me: Make this your provision, and do not enter Baghdad to so-and-so—whom he named—and do not inform him of anything; rather return to us, to the town. Then some groups came to us and informed us that our companions had turned back from al-'Aqabah and gone toward Khurasan. Then, in the following year, he performed hajj and sent us a gift from the rarities of Khurasan. He remained there for a period, then died—may Allah have mercy on him.

key_terms.النَّاحِيَةِ: The region or quarter, used here for the sacred direction associated with seeking the Imam عليه السلام.
key_terms.الْفُقَهَاءَ: Jurists learned in religious law who debated the narrator.
key_terms.الْكُتُبَ الْأَرْبَعَةَ: The four revealed scriptures mentioned in the narration as sources of prior knowledge.
key_terms.خَاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينَ: Seal of the Prophets, meaning the final prophet after whom there is no prophet.
key_terms.خَلِيفَتُهُ: His successor or vicegerent after him.
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring here to Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الزَّمَانِ: The Master of the Age, a title of the Imam عليه السلام.
key_terms.وَصِيُّهُ: His designated legatee, referring to the divinely appointed successor after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith of Ghanim al-Hindi describe his search for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and recognition of the Imamate?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the journey of Ghanim al-Hindi, a learned man from India, who searched for the final Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله after finding his description in earlier scriptures. Through investigation, debate, and guidance from al-Husayn ibn Ishkib, he embraced Islam and came to recognize the wilayah of أمير المؤمنين عليّ بن أبي طالب عليه السلام and the line of the Imams, eventually meeting Sahib al-Zaman عليه السلام.
